summary: Electric aircraft and counter-drone systems spanning capture, interception, cargo and control.
editor_note: Rather than selling one airframe, the company is assembling a coordinated counter-drone stack: a mothership, net capture, compact and launcher-based interceptors, autonomy and external sensing are designed to work together. Three prototype transition-flight demonstrations make the engineering thesis inspectable. Several systems are still scheduled through 2027, so production, export approvals, mission reliability and customer deployment remain the decisive tests.
investors: Sazze Partners, Stonebridge Ventures, Industrial Bank of Korea

product_evidence.claim: The official portfolio presents Mothership, Capture, Interceptor and Cargo systems with shared command-and-control and autonomy capabilities.
The financing announcement names the AB-U10, AB-U60, AB-U2 and AB-U4L, and reports transition-flight demonstrations across three prototypes completed in December 2025.
The first counter-UAS systems remain on staged commercialization timelines through 2027 rather than being evidenced as broadly deployed products.

market_context.primary_user: Military, public-safety and infrastructure operators evaluating counter-drone and autonomous aerial systems.
market_context.differentiation: Multiple high-speed electric airframes are designed as one detection, interception and assessment system instead of isolated drones.
market_context.why_now: The Series A supports commercialization, manufacturing capacity and international deployment after prototype transition-flight demonstrations.

risks.claim: Most of the portfolio is early or scheduled; production yield, mission reliability, procurement cycles, export controls and deployment economics remain unproven at scale.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment based on Airbility's official product surface and financing announcement.
